generated_by: services/evidence -- bundle.py, plus two report artifacts vendored from a local eval run
source: eval/data/reports-astscan/, produced by `ares scan --ast-scan true` against eval/data/staging/
notes: WHY THESE ARE COMMITTED AT ALL: eval/data/ is entirely gitignored -- `git ls-files eval/data/` returns 0 files. Without vendoring real artifacts here, every test that exercises a genuine report would skip in CI, and a green run would mean 'not checked' rather than 'correct'. This is the same reasoning as services/cve/snapshot/.

The two reports are byte-for-byte copies, renamed only. They were checked for absolute paths and home directories before vendoring: both contain relative paths only, so nothing about a developer's machine is published here.

ares-report-suppressed-only.json is the load-bearing fixture. It has 0 findings and 1 suppressed finding, a trailing separator on target.source_path, MIXED separators inside a single path value ('eval/data/staging/x/src\lib.rs'), and a title that ends with the raw location.file -- the scan.rs:237 case that affects 352 of the 1296 findings in the local corpus. A normalizer that handles only the path-typed fields fails on it.
ares-report-sixteen-findings.json exercises a non-trivial tree (16 leaves, depth 4) and the location.file == source_path case that projects to a literal '.'.

The .evidence.json bundles are regenerated by `python bundle.py vectors/<report> --force`. test_vectors.py asserts the regenerated bytes equal the committed bytes, so a code change that alters a root cannot pass by quietly refreshing the fixture -- pinned_values above is checked against the bundle contents as well.

not_checked_by_ci: the 636-report local corpus these two came from is NOT committed and NOT available in CI. test_vectors.py sweeps it only when eval/data/reports-astscan/ happens to exist locally, and its skip reason says so. Any figure quoted from that corpus in README.md is a dated local measurement, not a CI-verified one.

merkle_vectors.json is the cross-language contract. It was produced by two independent implementations of the RFC 6962 recurrence -- a recursive transcription of section 2.1 and the iterative stack-based builder -- which were required to agree for n = 0..33 before any value was written here. The Rust spec crate under onchain/spec/ and scripts/evidence-pda-vectors.test.ts assert against this same file; since nothing may be added to the core/ cargo workspace, a shared vector file is the only mechanism available for proving the three implementations agree.

pda_vectors.json pins Solana PDA derivation for the evidence_registry seeds. It was produced by anchor_payload.py, whose ed25519 on-curve test is hand-rolled from RFC 8032 in pure stdlib Python -- exactly the kind of code that is subtly wrong and still passes its author's own tests. scripts/evidence-pda-vectors.test.ts checks every case against @solana/web3.js's PublicKey.findProgramAddressSync, an implementation nobody in this repo wrote, and that cross-check is what makes the hand-rolled arithmetic acceptable. One case ('all-ones') resolves to bump 253, so the on-curve rejection demonstrably fires; without it the whole set would pass even if is_on_curve always returned False.

The two .evidence.json bundles were regenerated 2026-08-19 after bundle.py's volatile block gained a confirmed_at key (following ReportMetadata.confirmed_at landing in ares-core). Neither report was ever confirmed, so confirmed_at is null in both -- the merkle_root, commitment and leaf_count in pinned_values above are UNCHANGED, which is the design invariant working as intended: confirmed_at is metadata, hashed into no leaf and no commitment field, exactly like generated_at.

CRLF corruption, found and fixed 2026-08-19: this repo has core.autocrlf=true and no .gitattributes anywhere, so a plain Windows `git checkout` silently rewrites every LF in a tracked text file to CRLF in the working tree while `git status`/`git diff` report no change (git's comparison normalizes line endings before comparing). That corrupted every file in this directory after a branch-switch-and-merge sequence, and test_vectors.py's manifest-integrity suite caught it immediately -- byte-exact digests are exactly what this corruption breaks. Separately, merkle_vectors.json and pda_vectors.json were originally generated via shell stdout redirection rather than Path.write_bytes(), which (on this machine) introduced CRLF into them BEFORE they were ever committed; git's own commit-time clean filter silently normalized that back to LF on the way into the repo, so the committed blobs were always correct, but the bytes/sha256 recorded in this manifest had been measured on the pre-commit, CRLF-tainted files and were wrong for those two entries specifically (off by exactly the CRLF count: 134 and 47 bytes respectively). Both entries above are now the digest of the actual committed blob, verified via `git cat-file -p HEAD:<path>`. services/evidence/.gitattributes now marks every file in this directory `-text` so git never touches these bytes in either direction again. services/cve/snapshot/advisories.json was found to have the identical working-tree corruption on this same machine at the same time -- that is a pre-existing, repo-wide exposure this task did not fix, since it is outside services/evidence/.
